The app is now available in English — a Language switch in Settings → Appearance (Русский/English), independent of the system language. The whole interface is translated, including this changelog.

Manual category correction for Movie/Cartoon and TV Show/Cartoon Series — if the .nfo genre is empty or imprecise and a title ends up under the wrong tab, you can now fix it by hand: the category chip on its page opens a choice between the two options, or a reset back to automatic genre-based detection. A manual choice persists and survives future library rescans.

History now opens as a tab inside the library (swipe next to Library/Collections/Lists), styled the same way — it used to open as a separate screen.\n\nThe top bar now smoothly hides on scroll-down and returns on scroll-up on every screen in the app (movie/show page, Downloads, History, all settings sections), not just the library.

Downloads are now saved to the public Download/HomeCinema folder (visible in any file manager, survives clearing the app's data and even uninstalling it) instead of the app's private cache, which Android sometimes clears on its own — that was the actual cause of downloaded movies disappearing before. Alongside the video, matching .nfo and subtitle files are now downloaded too, each title in its own named folder.

Settings → Storage — you can point downloads at your own folder (via the system picker, including an SD card) instead of the default location; the same screen shows exactly where downloads are currently being saved.

Downloads — long-pressing a card turns on multi-select, so you can delete several titles at once or select them all.

Continue Watching moved into its own bar above the bottom navigation (thumbnail, title, resume button) instead of a row inside the top bar — it used to slide away and back together with the bar on scroll.

Fixed: the Delete button on a downloaded title's status pill got clipped when space was tight.

Playback notification mini-player — playing something in the internal player now shows a system notification with a poster and play/pause controls; tapping it jumps straight back into that title, even if the app had been fully closed.

The top bar now smoothly hides on scroll-down and returns on scroll-up, freeing up more room for cards.

On the root tabs (Library/Collections/Lists with no search or open collection), the back button/gesture now needs a second press within 2 seconds to actually exit — protection against closing the app by accident.

Downloads now shows posters as a grid, like the main library — tapping a card opens the movie/episode's page, which already has internal and external playback plus deleting the download.

Library — tapping the already-active Library tab again opens a quick type picker: Movies/TV Shows/Cartoons/Cartoon Series (only categories that actually exist on disk are shown).

Swiping between library tabs is no longer intercepted by the system back gesture on phones with gesture navigation — a swipe too close to the edge used to sometimes background the app instead of switching tabs.

A light vibration during library scrolling as the index passes each letter of the alphabet.

Floating bars (top and bottom) now sit flush against the top and bottom edges of the screen — there used to be an empty gap.

External playback for downloaded titles is now available from the title's own page (alongside the Downloads grid redesign).

The external-player playback notification now closes automatically when the app is closed (swiped away from Recents) — it used to linger until the 6-hour safety timeout or a manual Stop tap.

Important fix: rescanning the library (including the automatic nightly one) reset the Favorite flag on every title. If you ever lost your favorites before, this was the cause — the flag no longer gets cleared.

New navigation — the Library/Collections/Lists/History tabs moved to the bottom of the screen, within thumb reach; the logo, search, filters, downloads, library refresh, and settings stayed at the top. A Classic/New switch lives in Settings → Appearance → Library navigation, so you can go back to the old layout any time. Every bar (top and bottom) now shares the same floating look: inset from the screen edges (matters on phones with strongly rounded corners) and real glass blur in the Glass theme.

Continue Watching and History now also work for external playback, not just the internal player — previously only what you watched inside the app ended up there. Internal-playback history is now recorded immediately too, instead of after a few seconds' delay.

Continue Watching also launches the external player when it's set to Always external — it used to always open the internal player regardless of that setting.

An empty list (e.g. an empty Favorites) no longer suggests "scan your library" — that message never fit a simply-empty list.

The "rescan your library" hint after an app update now only appears when the new version actually added new .nfo fields — it used to show up after every single update, even ones with nothing new to scan for.

The changelog and the pre-install "what's new" dialog are now formatted as a bulleted list instead of one solid paragraph.

Fixed: the "found N titles" counter after a scan counted every episode of a show as its own title, inflating the number; the update check only ran on a cold start, not when returning to the foreground; the version changelog dialog gave no hint that its text could be scrolled further; the external-player playback notification didn't open the app when tapped and had no way to dismiss it manually before the 6-hour safety timeout.

Russian #tag search now understands almost any everyday word ("рыцарь"/knight, "вампир"/vampire, etc.), not just the ~800 pre-built ones — the dictionary grew to ~40,000 words (source: FreeDict/Wiktionary).

Library scanning — the "Parsing X/Y" counter now only counts what will actually become its own card; "Scanning folders on disk" now grows as the scan progresses and counts only videos, not .nfo/subtitle/image files too.

The external player picker in Settings no longer shows only system apps — Android was hiding third-party players (MX Player, etc.) without a manifest declaration, which is now in place.

Player — removed the duplicate settings gear: subtitles and audio tracks now live only in the native player controls, no second hand-rolled one on top.

Movie page — the Watch/External/Download buttons now share one size and style; year/rating/runtime/country/age rating/quality are now separate labeled pills with icons instead of one truncating line of text; a subtitle-availability badge was added.

Landscape orientation — the grid column count (Library, Collections, Lists) now adapts to the screen's width and height instead of staying fixed — cards no longer spill off the edge of the screen.

Fixed: switching between Library/Collections/Lists tabs could fail to register when skipping over a tab; the scroll-to-top/bottom buttons were redrawn (on some devices the round shadowed button rendered as a polygon instead of a circle).

Fixed card jitter while scrolling the library. Cause: the alphabet rail on the right sometimes appeared and disappeared during ordinary vertical scrolling (not just during a swipe between tabs, which is what that hiding behavior was originally built for), which kept changing the card grid\'s width.

Subtitles — .srt/.ass/.ssa/.sub/.vtt files next to a video now attach automatically, in the internal player (both SMB streaming and a downloaded file) and in an external one (passed via launch parameters, if the player supports it).

Watch history — a new screen (icon in the library header) with everything you've watched, including already-finished titles.

External player choice — in Settings → Playback you can pin a specific app instead of choosing every time.

Rescan hint — after an update that adds new .nfo fields, you're now offered a library rescan.

Small fixes: a duplicate "External player" button in the episode list, the alphabet rail flickering during a tab swipe, the external-player button's color/size on a movie card, a standalone subtitles button in the internal player that lingered even without subtitles — subtitles and audio track are now together in one settings icon.

Actor filmography — tapping an actor's name on a movie page now opens a list of their other titles, same as it already did for directors. Names with no other titles in your library are no longer highlighted or clickable, so they don't look misleadingly tappable.

New .nfo fields on the movie page: tagline, studio, age rating.

Release quality (e.g. "1080p BDRip"), detected from the filename and shown next to the year and rating.

External playback now tries to resume from the saved position (not supported by every player).

Tag search now understands Russian. Values of the .nfo <tag> field are almost always in English (heist, pirates, etc.) — you can now type "#ограбление" or "#пираты" in Russian, and it\'s silently translated and matched against the English tags in the background, with no change needed to how you type the query.

The changelog now works offline — it used to load the version list from GitHub and was unavailable without a connection. Each version is now collapsed by default so the list doesn\'t stretch out too long.\n\nThe Glass theme\'s background color swatches are brighter and more distinct now.

Settings redesigned. Instead of one long list, there\'s now a compact list of sections (Sources, Library, Playback, Appearance, Storage, Changelog, About) — each with a short subtitle showing its current value. Tapping one opens that section\'s own screen.
Search history. Opening search with an empty field now shows a list of recent queries — tap one to reuse it, remove a specific entry, or clear the whole history at once.
Swipe between library tabs. You can now switch between Library, Collections, and Lists with a left/right swipe across the screen, not just by tapping a tab.

Glass theme opacity control — a "Glass opacity" slider (40–95%) was added to Settings. Panels used to be a fixed level of translucency that made arrows and text hard to make out — now you can make them read more clearly.\n\nGlass theme background color choice — 6 ready-made presets (indigo, charcoal, midnight blue, emerald, wine, black) instead of one fixed color.

Critical fix: external-player playback finally stopped cutting out after a few minutes. The real cause: MX Player doesn\'t keep one connection open the whole time — it downloads data in short local-network bursts and plays for long stretches from its own already-downloaded buffer. The internal safety timer was raised from 5 minutes to 6 hours.

App updates can now be downloaded and installed right from within the app. When a new version is available, the banner gets a Details button showing the changelog and letting you decide whether to install. The Install button downloads the APK inside the app and immediately offers to install it — no more manually visiting the GitHub page.
External playback (e.g. MX Player) no longer cuts out after ~5 minutes with a "Cannot play this link" error.

Adaptive title font size in the library grid — long titles now shrink to fit instead of getting cut off with an ellipsis.

Original title — if present in the .nfo, it's shown under the localized title on the movie page (e.g. "Venom (Веном)").

Director filmography — tapping a director's name on a movie page opens a list of their other titles from your library.

Fix: resolved a hidden bug where bottom sheets (filters, add to list) could render at zero height in the Glass theme.

Glass: real background blur. The Glass theme now uses real backdrop blur (the Haze library) instead of a flat translucent fill — the top bar, tabs, settings cards, and bottom sheets genuinely blur whatever scrolls behind them.\n\nImportant: minimum Android version raised to 12 (API 31) — real backdrop blur is technically impossible on older versions even with third-party libraries, so there was no point keeping two different looks around.

Custom lists (playlists) — create, rename, delete, and add or remove any movies/shows.

Favorites — a quick heart toggle on a movie's page, plus a badge on its poster.

A Changelog section in Settings — the version list pulled straight from GitHub Releases.

Fixed playback in external players other than VLC (e.g. KMPlayer) — the player used to open but couldn\'t read the file unless it had already been downloaded.\n\nSearch by .nfo hashtags (e.g. #pirates). Sort by rating. Per-category title counts in the filters. A warning when search is running with a forgotten active filter. The header logo resets filters/search. On the movie page — other parts of the same collection shown at the bottom.

Downloads and automatic library refresh moved to WorkManager — they survive the app being closed, resuming continues from where it left off instead of starting over, and a progress notification is shown.

Clear connection/scanning error messages (wrong password, host unreachable, share not found) instead of raw technical text.

The app now checks GitHub for a new version on launch by itself. SMB scanning was sped up and fixed on real devices, and an app icon was added. The About section was updated.
